## Explanations

### Warm-up

First a quick look back: **b p m f** with **a**, in all four tones.

**bā** · **bá** · **bǎ** · **bà**  
**pā** · **pá** · **pǎ** · **pà**  
**mā** (mum) · **má** (hemp) · **mǎ** (horse) · **mà** (to scold)  
**fā** · **fá** · **fǎ** · **fà**  

### d and t: the puff again

It works like b and p: **t** has a strong puff of air (English *top*), **d** has none (the *t* in English *stop*).

**n** and **l** are the same as in English and German.

**dā** · **tā**  
**dà** · **tà**  
**nà** · **là**  

### 2nd or 3rd?

The pair beginners mix up most is the **2nd** tone (rising) and the **3rd** (low). Said on its own, the 3rd tone can rise a little at the end, so both seem to go up.

Listen to where they **start**: the 2nd starts in the middle and climbs straight up, like a surprised *What?* The 3rd first sinks low and stays there, like a doubtful *Hmm…*

Each row is 2nd, then 3rd.

**dá** · **dǎ**  
**ná** · **nǎ**  
**má** (hemp) · **mǎ** (horse)  

### Your second block of the chart

da ta na la in all four tones. Play each row and draw the shapes in the air with your hand: high, rising, low, falling.

| | 1st tone | 2nd tone | 3rd tone | 4th tone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **da** | dā | dá | dǎ | dà |
| **ta** | tā | tá | tǎ | tà |
| **na** | nā | ná | nǎ | nà |
| **la** | lā | lá | lǎ | là |

## New words

| Pinyin | Meaning | Note |
|--------|---------|------|
| **tā**<br><sub>ta1</sub> | he / she | One word for he and she (and him and her). Only the characters differ. |
| **dà**<br><sub>da4</sub> | big | No puff of air on the d, like the t in English stop. |
| **nà**<br><sub>na4</sub> | that | Falling, like pointing: that one! |
| **nǎ**<br><sub>na3</sub> | which? | Low. Only the tone tells nǎ (which?) from nà (that). |

## New phrases

| Pinyin | English | Literally |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| **Tā pà.**<br><sub>Ta1 pa4.</sub> | He / she is scared. | he / afraid |
| **Tā bàba pà.**<br><sub>Ta1 ba4ba5 pa4.</sub> | His / her dad is scared. | he / dad / afraid |
